rationale: Parkinson inpatient mixed vegetarian menu listed parsley; UPDRS III total improved but individual herb intake, drying and stride-length changes were not reported.
access_or_open: Local full primary PMC7072275 and appendix; original single-food controlled stride comparisons open.

rationale: Oral common chive leaf extract in stroke-model mice had neurological and Morris water-maze outcomes; abstract contains no anxiety result. Ferulic acid studies are isolated constituent rather than dried chives.
access_or_open: Primary PMID29933243 abstract accessible; full numerical anxiety endpoint if any remains unverified.

rationale: Parsley appeared in a mixed Parkinson diet menu; no assigned fresh-leaf exposure or separate hand dexterity or finger-tapping item results appear.
access_or_open: Full body and appendix local; single-herb clinical hand-task studies open.

rationale: Morris water-maze and neurological severity outcomes after oral common chive extract in ischemic mice do not supply a clinical executive-function contrast or fresh chive ingestion effect.
access_or_open: PMID29933243 abstract accessible; full numerical executive-task outcome not confirmed.

rationale: Two closely related bay-odor reports found better late visual vigilance at the lower odor load in healthy men. The earlier 11-person comparison reported p=.026 across 30 minutes and the later nine-person comparison recorded 93.8% versus 88.0% at 30 minutes. The high odor load showed no clear accuracy benefit and the samples may overlap. The exposure was inhaled; effects of eating ground bay leaf on Parkinson attention remain open.
access_or_open: 2011 and earlier Japanese originals recovered. Their low-load vigilance results align and possible cohort overlap remains unresolved.

rationale: Dried identified dill leaf capsules versus starch in 42 adults with diabetes: any esophageal complaint 3/21 to 5/21 versus 5/21 to 5/21; no drooling or salivary-flow measurement and no Parkinson subgroup.
access_or_open: Full article locally available as research/2020-2024/Source-Text/PMC7275438.txt; separate leaf-specific drooling outcome still open.

rationale: Curry-leaf extracts tested in drug-induced rodent involuntary chewing and tongue movements, which are distinct from reduced facial expressivity; cooked whole leaves and patient item 3.2 were not tested.
access_or_open: 2012 primary full body research/2010-2014/Source-Text/PMC3832166.txt; individual clinical expression results open.

rationale: Mixed Parkinson vegetarian diet listed lovage as seasoning, but exposure form and individual intake were unspecified and freezing episodes were not reported; total motor score does not resolve the leaf's effect.
access_or_open: Local full primary PMC7072275 and appendix; dried lovage versus freezing-specific observations open.

rationale: Cardamom is listed in a multicomponent Parkinson diet; reported total motor scores cannot establish a rest-tremor item response or cardamom attribution.
access_or_open: Original individual item data and actual consumption remain open.

rationale: Infant poisoning involved green anise and star anise in a mixed infusion with neurological symptoms; seed identity, age, dose, coexposure and outcome differ from target.
access_or_open: No quantified visual hallucination frequency attributed to ground Pimpinella anisum found.

rationale: The dried-thyme trial measures self-rated memory. Oral isolated-thymol studies in juvenile rats report behavioral effects, including increased Y-maze alternation. These outcomes do not identify a fresh culinary thyme effect on Parkinson attention.
access_or_open: Full 2023 paper and NCT05987228 registry accessible; attention-specific or fresh-food controlled comparisons open.

rationale: Mixed Parkinson vegetarian menu lists chervil without plant dose or fresh preparation; total UPDRS III is not an individual rigidity result.
access_or_open: Local PMC7072275 and appendix; isolated fresh garden chervil rigidity comparison open.

rationale: Capsaicin altered rat general motor activity under pharmacological conditions; this is neither measured Parkinson walking slowness nor smoked paprika ingestion.
access_or_open: Preserve different locomotion and levodopa-induced dyskinesia endpoints; no direct smoked-food contrast found.

rationale: The author abstract reports fewer abnormal involuntary movements after injected isolated capsaicin in lesioned rats. It leaves the levodopa regimen and scoring protocol unverified. A separate study found lower spontaneous and drug-elicited movement, making general activity suppression a competing explanation. Ground paprika capsaicinoid content varies, and no Parkinson dyskinesia direction can be assigned to oral ground paprika.
access_or_open: PMC2036408 historical issue remains body-access pending; normal locomotion experiments are not dyskinesia measures.

rationale: Nigella oil was studied in healthy mouse pellet-reaching learning, a task adjacent to dexterity; oil, healthy animals and unroasted preparation differ from toasted whole seed and Parkinson impairment.
access_or_open: Seek human Parkinson manual-dexterity comparisons with verified toasted Nigella sativa seed.

rationale: Cinnamon appears in mixed Parkinson meal plans; MDS-UPDRS part II composite is reported without a separate handwriting comparison or isolated ground-cinnamon effect.
access_or_open: Seek item-level tables and participant-specific consumption; no direct handwriting contrast established.

rationale: The green-cardamom extract animal experiment measures drug-induced sleep. Acute and repeated black-cardamom extract reports share one registration and measure timed cognitive tasks with no daytime sleepiness scale. The results do not establish a daytime symptom direction after eating ground cardamom.
access_or_open: No matched daytime symptom comparison identified; distinguish sedation and sleep induction.

rationale: Topical allyl isothiocyanate in rats elicits swallows; a constituent applied to the swallowing apparatus is not eaten ground mustard seed or a patient dysphagia outcome.
access_or_open: Underlying historical white-mustard letter remains separate from reviewed journal index; clinical seed-specific swallowing outcome remains open.

rationale: 2024 Parkinson trial saffron capsule versus placebo reported MDS-UPDRS III total interaction F=0.53, p=0.424; accessible report does not provide facial-expression item 3.2.
access_or_open: Original item-level data and fresh culinary ground-spice exposure remain open; NCT05696665 is a mixed saffron/chamomile protocol.

rationale: The small hot-sauce and mustard meal study tests a mixture. The separate cannabinol insomnia trial uses a paprika colorant in its formulation, with the comparison varying cannabinol. No study gives a ground-paprika comparison for Parkinson insomnia.
access_or_open: CBN trial https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13357646/ and NCT05344170; no direct paprika versus no-paprika insomnia comparison found.

rationale: Whole hazelnuts appear on a mixed Parkinson diet menu. The published motor total includes rest tremor, with no individual rest-tremor estimate. The plan lists separate oils and gives no cold-pressed hazelnut-oil exposure contrast.
access_or_open: Seek a measured Parkinson rest-tremor comparison with confirmed hazelnut oil grade and intake. Whole nuts, isolated constituents, and action tremor remain adjacent.

rationale: The randomized Parkinson diet trial lists canola among low-fat plan ingredients and reports motor sums with speech items. No arm-level acoustic volume or isolated canola exposure is published. A primary oral olive-oil challenge used canola as diluent and recorded throat symptoms without measuring vocal intensity.
access_or_open: Recover any individual speech or acoustic outcomes and oil grade. The case report records acute sensitivity within an olive blend.

rationale: A synuclein mouse study reports forepaw stride variability of 15.76% with control diet and 10.18% with curcumin. Each diet contained the same amount of soybean oil. The Angelman-model experiment also held soybean oil constant between two blends. A separate ordinal stepping comparison uses spinal injury and provides no stride distance.
access_or_open: Seek an isolated refined-oil contrast with measured stride length. Variability, stride length and ordinal stepping are different outcomes.

rationale: The prospective cohort pooled refined and pomace oil. The fully adjusted attention estimate was −0.006 z-score units per 10 g/day (95% CI −0.047 to 0.035), with an attenuated top-tertile comparison. A refined-oil trial gives an inconclusive 1-back activation interaction. Observational usual cooking-oil exposure and common olive-oil vehicles do not isolate a refined-oil attention effect in Parkinson disease.
access_or_open: Two pediatric comparator items, broad review contexts, and individual registry results remain unresolved. The oil-grade split and a dedicated Parkinson attention measure remain open.
